original_question: For unbounded linear operators A(t) on a Banach space X and for a starting time t0 , characterize the well-posedness of the non-autonomous Cauchy problem ẋ(t) = A(t)x(t) for t ≥ t0 x(t0 ) = x0 by Hille-Yosida type condition for an operator G generating an evolution semigroup on X = C0 (R, X) or X = Lp (R, X).
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s official open problem very closely: it has the family of unbounded operators A(t) on a Banach space, the starting time t0, the non-autonomous Cauchy problem x'(t)=A(t)x(t) for t≥t0 with x(t0)=x0, and the aim of characterizing well-posedness by a Hille–Yosida-type condition for an operator G generating an evolution semigroup on C_0(R,X) or L^p(R,X). ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, the underlying Banach space and the function-space state space should be notationally separated; as written, X is used both for the base space and again for C_0(R,X) or L^p(R,X).

The initial datum should be quantified explicitly as x0 in the underlying Banach space, and the time interval should be stated as t≥t0 for the chosen starting time t0. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))

The role of G should be stated more precisely: the paper asks for a Hille–Yosida-type condition on an operator G generating the associated evolution semigroup on the specified function space, not on an arbitrary auxiliary operator. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))

The paper does not add extra hypotheses here on measurability or continuity of t↦A(t), common domains D(A(t)), or the admissible range of p; a faithful rewrite should therefore avoid inserting such additional assumptions unless clearly marked as explanatory rather than part of the paper’s statement. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))

The paper also does not impose a real-versus-complex scalar-field restriction in the statement of this problem, so a paper-faithful rewrite should not add one. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))
The target is an open problem in a collected list of unsolved semigroup-theoretic questions, not a theorem, proposition, or conjecture. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00416))

The paper does not provide an explicit equivalent reformulation of Problem 8 nearby, so the rewrite should stay with the original Hille–Yosida/evolution-semigroup formulation. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))
refined_question: Let E be a Banach space, let t0 be an initial time, and let (A(t)) be a family of unbounded linear operators on E. Characterize, by a Hille–Yosida-type condition on an operator G generating the associated evolution semigroup on either C_0(R,E) or L^p(R,E), when the non-autonomous abstract Cauchy problem x'(t)=A(t)x(t) for t≥t0 with x(t0)=x0, x0∈E, is well posed. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2410.00416v2))
justification: This is exactly the paper’s Problem 8 in Section 1. Your draft is already close to verbatim; the main repairs needed are notational and scoping repairs: disentangle the base Banach space from the function-space state space, make the initial datum explicit, and keep the focus on a Hille–Yosida-type characterization via the generator of an evolution semigroup on the two ambient spaces named in the paper. I did not add domain regularity, measurability, common-domain hypotheses, or a specific formula for G, because those are not part of the paper’s official statement of this open problem. The abstract confirms that the paper is a curated collection of open problems, so the correct target is an open problem rather than a theorem or conjecture. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00416))
